Greed mostly. Everyone along the supply chain is upping prices while they simultaneously lower quality. Combined with the deflated buying power of the US dollar and you have a perfect storm of rising prices and falling quality/quantity. They tested the waters with this back in the mid-2000s with hurricane Katrina pumping up gas prices. All the food manufacturers said the cost of diesel for the trucks that ship the food around was too high and they had to raise prices and/or lower quantities/portions to offset the cost. Items that were previously sold in packs of 12 went to packs of 10. One pound packages became 12 ounce packages. 96 fl ounces went to 92 then to 87 then to 83. The sizes shrink and the prices grow. Fast food is no exception to this. They skimp on ingredients, alter recipes, introduce "new" sizes and rearrange combos to obscure the fact that the once cheap food is now as expensive as a healthy home cooked meal for two. Gas prices have dropped significantly now but the prices keep going up, proof that the story was just a cover for raising prices long term. As always though we have ourselves to blame for all this.
